title: Choose the visual world for Matpris
question: The roll assigned Shelf Edge. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Shelf Edge
options.lineage: Swedish shelf-edge price labels (hyllkantsetiketter) and their jmf-pris line
options.thesis: Every result is a real shelf label, ranked by the jmf-pris shoppers already read in store.
options.viewport: Charcoal rail header with one wide search and location strip; left, results hang as labels on shelf rails, cheapest on the yellow label; right, the map.
options.risk: Shelf yellow and red can read like a discount flyer if they spread beyond offers and the answer.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale alone: no card boxes; the price numeral is huge and every other line is small.
Nothing labelled twice: the chain logo sits on the label once; store and distance are one line.
The chain filter is a rail whose segments are as wide as each chain's share of the results.
Pointing at a label lifts its store pin and dims every other pin.

options.label: Test Table
options.lineage: Swedish consumer-magazine product tests and their ranked tables
options.thesis: Each search reads as a consumer test: ranked rows, shown working, a Bäst i test mark on the winner.
options.viewport: A white sheet: the winner row in a framed result box with the red roundel, a sortable ranked table below, map beside.
options.risk: Familiar: a ranked table is close to where most price sites already land.

options.label: Orienteering Course
options.lineage: ISOM orienteering maps, O-ringen control descriptions
options.thesis: The trip to the cheapest store as an orienteering course: stores are controls, purple marks only the chosen leg.
options.viewport: Map leads at two thirds width with purple course to the cheapest store; the results list is a control description sheet beside it.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and Swedes know these maps; holds audience identification, loses on price clarity.
options.risk: Map-first: the price comparison becomes the legend instead of the answer.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.viewport: Folded inlay with side A and side B lists.
options.case: Shoppers don't identify with it and handwriting hurts price reading.
options.kept: Right-aligned tabular figures held tight to one margin.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.viewport: Tab rail down the edge, one board per chain.
options.case: Loses both axes: a manual's ply system has nothing to do with groceries.
options.kept: Tabs sized by extent: the chain filter shows each chain's share.

options.label: Streaming Wall
options.thesis: Products as poster tiles in rows per chain.
options.viewport: Horizontal rows of product tiles per chain.
options.case: Horizontal rows hide the comparison; loses both axes.
options.kept: Focus on one item and everything else steps back.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Prices as a coded pulse plot.
options.viewport: A black field with one white line stack.
options.case: Coding hides the facts shoppers need to trust; loses both axes.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.viewport: One giant numeral with axis sliders.
options.case: A type demo, not a shopping tool; loses both axes.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone, no boxes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A price-comparison app as the category ships it, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Search bar on top, result cards with thumbnails on the left, the map on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
